editorial.headline: When a Building’s Structure Demands More Than a Surface Repair
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the specialist structural work that supports, corrects, strengthens, and even moves entire buildings and civil structures.
editorial.body:
KBLI 2025 43901 concerns the installation and engineering of building structures: work done where the integrity, position, or capacity of a structure itself is at issue. It includes installing foundations and piles; concrete pouring and foundation reinforcement for buildings, roads and bridges, waterworks, jetties, offshore structures, and similar works within building and civil-construction projects. Its scope is therefore structural rather than cosmetic, concerned with the elements that allow a built asset to stand, carry load, and perform as intended.

The activity also reaches the difficult interventions that arise after construction. It covers correcting tilting, shifting, and settlement in building and civil structures; moving, rotating, or elevating an entire structure intact, including heritage buildings; and strengthening a structure to increase capacity, introduce seismic retrofitting, or support a change of use. Replacing critical principal structural elements—including columns, beams, and slabs—also sits within the activity. The classification identifies the relevant construction-foundation sub-classification as KK001.

Registration is open at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. At the national level, the activity is TERBUKA to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That matters because the code’s scope is not a narrow maintenance label: it describes specialist work on foundations, structural defects, structural reinforcement, and major interventions to an existing built form. The national position is therefore plainly open rather than qualified by a lower foreign-equity cap.

Bali’s position is also open in the sense that this activity is not blocked by the province-wide PMA moratorium. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—and the record states that it is not blocked by that moratorium. The moratorium permanently blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI across Bali; this activity does not fall into that blocked position. For a foreign investor assessing the island specifically, the honest conclusion is that Bali does not impose the moratorium bar recorded for lower-risk activities here.
